title: Keep /cv and /en/cv at zero client JavaScript: production PDFs are printed from the PUBLISHED pages
body: functions/cv.pdf.ts and functions/en/cv.pdf.ts call functions/_handler.ts, which asks Cloudflare Browser Rendering to print the live /cv or /en/cv and waits for network idle (LOAD_WAIT in scripts/pdf-options.ts). Any script on those pages — a component with a <script>, an island, analytics added to src/layouts/Base.astro, a ClientRouter — changes the downloaded PDF silently in production. Only the reader pages may ship JS: the landing (index.html, en/index.html) and the brief view (brief/index.html, en/brief/index.html). The allowlist is PAGES_WITH_JS in scripts/pages-with-js.ts (SCROLL_DRIVEN_PAGES within it is the landing's scroll exception); adding a page there is an explicit decision that shows up in a diff, never a fix for a failing `pnpm run test:js`. Page scripts live in src/components/v2/Landing.astro and src/components/HomeDocument.astro, never in Base.astro or src/components/cv/** (shared with the CV pages).
not_derivable: The link between a script on /cv and a changed production PDF goes through Browser Rendering at request time; nothing in the CV page's code shows it.
